title: Maple Street Rising
premise: When Emrys Ravensworth transfers to Hollow Creek High, she notices the school hums at night and the oldest records simply stop in 1974. Paired with her nemesis, popular golden boy Theo Vance, for a semester history project, she discovers his family helped bury the truth: the school was built over a shuttered reform school whose students vanished. As Emrys and Theo's rivalry thaws into something tender, they must choose between protecting their families' legacies and exposing what the school board covered up — before the anniversary ceremony seals the archives forever. In the end, they publish the names of the lost students, Emrys claims her own hidden connection to the reform school, and Maple Street finally remembers.
about_author: Lena Underhill is a former substitute teacher who spent years collecting strange stories from empty hallways. She writes young adult mysteries about small towns that keep big secrets.

chapters.title: The New Kid Hears It Hum
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. On her first day at Hollow Creek High, Emrys maps every exit and feels a low vibration under the gym floor during assembly. A janitor warns her not to ask about the east wing. Emotional beat: wary curiosity — she's moved towns too many times to believe anywhere is safe.

chapters.title: Assigned to Your Worst Enemy
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Ms. Okafor pairs Emrys with Theo Vance for the semester-long 'Uncovering Local History' project worth half their grade. Their first library session devolves into insults until Emrys finds a 1974 photo showing students who don't appear in any yearbook. Beat: grudging alliance born of mutual ambition.

chapters.title: What the Yearbook Left Out
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Digging through microfilm, they find the school's predecessor: Ashford Reform School for Girls, closed abruptly in 1974 after a fire. Theo's grandfather's name appears on the closing board. Beat: first crack in Theo's certainty; Emrys feels the thrill of being right.

chapters.title: Theo's Family Portrait
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. At a Vance family dinner, Theo probes his grandfather about Ashford and gets a cold warning: some buildings fall so better ones can rise. His mother slides him an envelope of old board minutes to 'put it to rest.' Beat: loyalty pulling against conscience.

chapters.title: The Girl in the Basement Photograph
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The board minutes list eleven transferred students — ten accounted for, one missing: R. Calloway. Emrys recognizes the surname from her grandmother's letters back home. Beat: dread and personal stakes colliding; this is no longer just a project.

chapters.title: Detention in the East Wing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Caught sneaking into the sealed east wing, both get detention — which gives them unsupervised access. They find a bricked doorway behind lockers and scratch marks on the inside. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; the partnership turns real, almost tender.

chapters.title: Love Is a Liability
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. After a near-kiss interrupted by a security guard, Theo pulls away, terrified his family will destroy Emrys's scholarship prospects if they keep digging. They fight; he threatens to switch partners. Beat: love against duty — both hearts breaking over the same secret.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Deadline
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The school announces its 50th-anniversary gala where all archival materials will be ceremonially resealed. Theo learns his grandfather will attend as honored guest. He secretly copies the full minutes and leaves them in Emrys's locker. Beat: Theo chooses truth over blood.

chapters.title: Rosalind Calloway
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys confronts her grandmother and learns Rosalind Calloway was her great-aunt — a runaway from Ashford who survived because a Vance boy opened a door the night of the fire. The missing student was family; the buried hero was his. Beat: grief, fury, and a shared inheritance of guilt and courage.

chapters.title: Maple Street Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the gala, Emrys and Theo hijack the ceremony, reading the eleven names aloud as families in the crowd react — some weeping, one board member resigning on the spot. The archives stay open; a memorial garden is pledged. Emrys and Theo, hand in hand, finally feel like they belong somewhere. Beat: catharsis, justice, and love chosen freely.
